findings.title: Retry-count delete clause is not limited to SMS reminders
findings.body: The second OR branch has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` condition, so it matches reminders of any method (email, WhatsApp) whose `retryCount` is above 1. This is an SMS-only cron job, so it should not delete other methods' rows. Today only this job increments the count, which hides the problem. Any later use of `retryCount` by another method would make this job delete those reminders. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to that branch.

findings.title: Unguarded DB update inside catch can abort the whole loop
findings.body: The `prisma.workflowReminder.update` in the catch block is not wrapped in its own try/catch. If it throws, for example because the row was deleted concurrently or the database is unavailable, the exception leaves the handler. The remaining reminders are skipped and the cron request fails with a 500. The catch also counts failures after an SMS was already scheduled, such as a failing `update` that sets `scheduled: true`. In that case a retry can send the SMS twice. Wrap the increment in its own try/catch, and use `increment: 1` instead of a stale read-then-write value.
